Glossary lookup full ptx confirms an inherited human bankrupt/expense object; Jan uses assets/shops as affected objects. The explicit mzabnile restatement supports disposal, but not the machine reader’s stronger dissipate/liquidate implication.

The source has emphatic ṭ in mpaṭxile/mpaṭaxwolle against inherited t; spelling is retained. Form lookup matches ptx only under consonant-diacritic folding; this is suggestive, not a demonstrated sound correspondence.

mpaṭaxwolle in the army-depot sequence may be Preterit-wa with an l-agent. Its habitual English does not decide the morphology. Ammunition-taking is explicit, physical entry/breakage is not independently described; no unsupported break-into sense is published.
No collocation or light-verb-plus-noun construction is established. Selected English is supplied project machine translation.

Does the disposal use carry a conventional disparaging sense such as squander, or simply dispose of/sell? New2 avoids asserting a sale below value.

In 1.36/1521, confirm the agent lu ḥasyo and pronominal object in mpaṭxile. The quotation is an attributed account of disposal, not an independently verified transaction.
